{{short description|Subset of real numbers that are greater than zero}}

In [[mathematics]], the [[Set (mathematics)|set]] of '''positive real numbers''', <math>\R_{>0} = \left\{ x \in \R \mid x > 0 \right\},</math> is the subset of those [[real number]]s that are greater than zero. The '''non-negative real numbers''', <math>\R_{\geq 0} = \left\{ x \in \R \mid x \geq 0 \right\},</math> also include zero. Although the symbols <math>\R_{+}</math> and <math>\R^{+}</math> are ambiguously used for either of these, the notation <math>\R_{+}</math> or <math>\R^{+}</math> for <math>\left\{ x \in \R \mid x \geq 0 \right\}</math> and <math>\R_{+}^{*}</math> or <math>\R^{+}_{*}</math> for <math>\left\{ x \in \R \mid x > 0 \right\}</math> has also been widely employed, is aligned with the practice in algebra of denoting the exclusion of the zero element with a star, and should be understandable to most practicing mathematicians.<ref>{{Cite web|title=positive number in nLab|url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/positive+number|access-date=2020-08-11|website=ncatlab.org}}</ref>

In a [[complex plane]], <math>\R_{>0}</math> is identified with the '''positive real axis''' (or '''positive real half-axis'''), and is usually drawn as a horizontal [[Ray (geometry)|ray]]. This ray is used as reference in the [[Complex number#Polar form|polar form of a complex number]]. The real positive axis corresponds to [[complex number]]s <math>z = |z| \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\varphi},</math> with [[Argument (complex analysis)|argument]] <math>\varphi = 0.</math>

==Properties==
The set <math>\R_{>0}</math> is [[Closure (mathematics)|closed]] under addition, multiplication, and division. It inherits a [[topology]] from the [[real line]] and, thus, has the structure of a multiplicative [[topological group]] or of an additive [[topological semigroup]].

For a given positive real number <math>x,</math> the [[sequence]] <math>\left\{x^n\right\}</math> of its integral powers has three different fates: When <math>x \in (0, 1),</math> the [[Limit (mathematics)|limit]] is zero; when <math>x = 1,</math> the sequence is constant; and when <math>x > 1,</math> the sequence is [[Unbounded set|unbounded]].

<math>\R_{>0} = (0,1) \cup \{ 1 \} \cup (1,\infty)</math> and the [[multiplicative inverse]] function exchanges the intervals. The functions [[Floor function|floor]], <math>\operatorname{floor} : [ 1 , \infty ) \to \N,\, x \mapsto \lfloor x \rfloor,</math> and [[Sawtooth function|excess]], <math>\operatorname{excess} : [ 1 , \infty ) \to (0,1),\, x \mapsto x - \lfloor x \rfloor,</math> have been used to describe an element <math>x \in \R_{>0}</math> as a [[continued fraction]] <math>\left[ n_0; n_1, n_2, \ldots\right],</math> which is a sequence of integers obtained from the floor function after the excess has been reciprocated. For rational <math>x,</math> the sequence terminates with an exact fractional expression of <math>x,</math> and for [[quadratic irrational]] <math>x,</math> the sequence becomes a [[periodic continued fraction]].

The ordered set <math>\left(\R_{>0}, >\right)</math> forms a [[total order]] but is {{em|not}} a [[well-ordered set]]. The [[doubly infinite]] [[geometric progression]] <math>10^n,</math> where <math>n</math> is an [[integer]], lies entirely in <math>\left(\R_{>0}, >\right)</math> and serves  to section it for access. <math>\R_{>0}</math> forms a '''ratio scale''', the highest [[level of measurement]]. Elements may be written in [[scientific notation]] as <math>a \times 10^b,</math> where <math>1 \leq a < 10</math> and <math>b</math> is the integer in the doubly infinite progression, and is called the [[Decade (log scale)|decade]]. In the study of physical magnitudes, the order of decades  provides positive and  negative ordinals referring to an ordinal scale implicit in the ratio scale.

In the study of [[classical group]]s, for every <math>n \in \N,</math> the [[determinant]] gives a map from <math>n \times n</math> matrices over the reals to the real numbers: <math>\mathrm{M}(n, \R) \to \R.</math> Restricting to invertible matrices gives a map from the [[general linear group]] to non-zero real numbers: <math>\mathrm{GL}(n, \R) \to \R^\times.</math> Restricting to matrices with a positive determinant gives the map <math>\operatorname{GL}^+(n, \R) \to \R_{> 0}</math>; interpreting the image as a [[quotient group]] by the [[normal subgroup]] <math>\operatorname{SL}(n, \R) \triangleleft \operatorname{GL}^+(n, \R),</math> called the [[special linear group]],  expresses the positive reals as a [[Lie group]].

==Ratio scale==
Among the [[levels of measurement]], the '''ratio scale''' provides the finest detail. The [[Division (mathematics)|division]] function  takes a value of one when [[numerator]] and [[denominator]] are  equal. Other ratios are compared to one by logarithms, often [[common logarithm]] using base 10. The ratio scale then segments by [[orders of magnitude]] used in science and technology, expressed in various [[units of measurement]].

An early expression of ratio scale was articulated geometrically by [[Eudoxus of Cnidus|Eudoxus]]: "it was ... in geometrical language that the general theory of [[Proportionality (mathematics)|proportion]] of Eudoxus was developed, which is equivalent to a theory of positive real  numbers."<ref>[[E. J. Dijksterhuis]] (1961) [https://archive.org/details/e.j.dijksterhuisthemechanizationoftheworldpictureoxforduniversitypress1961/page/n51/mode/2up Mechanization of the World-Picture], page 51, via [[Internet Archive]]</ref>

==Logarithmic measure==
If <math>[a,b] \subseteq \R_{>0}</math> is an [[Interval (mathematics)|interval]], then <math>\mu([a,b]) = \log(b / a) = \log 
b - \log a</math> determines a [[Measure (mathematics)|measure]] on certain subsets of <math>\R_{>0},</math> corresponding to the [[pullback]] of the usual [[Lebesgue measure]] on the real numbers under the logarithm: it is the length on the [[logarithmic scale]]. In fact, it is an [[invariant measure]] with respect to multiplication <math>[a,b] \to [az, bz]</math> by a <math>z \in \R_{>0},</math> just as the Lebesgue measure is invariant under addition. In the context of topological groups, this measure is an example of a [[Haar measure]].

The utility of this measure is shown in its use for describing [[stellar magnitude]]s and noise levels in [[decibel]]s, among other applications of the [[logarithmic scale]]. For purposes of international standards [[ISO 80000-3]], the dimensionless quantities are referred to as [[Level (logarithmic quantity)|levels]].

==Applications==
The non-negative reals serve as the [[Image of a function|image]] for [[Metric (mathematics)|metric]]s, [[Norm (mathematics)|norm]]s, and [[Measure (mathematics)|measure]]s in mathematics.

Including 0, the set <math>\R_{\geq 0}</math> has a [[semiring]] structure (0 being the [[additive identity]]), known as the [[probability semiring]]; taking logarithms (with a choice of base giving a [[logarithmic unit]]) gives an [[isomorphism]] with the [[log semiring]] (with 0 corresponding to <math>- \infty</math>), and its units (the finite numbers, excluding <math>- \infty</math>) correspond to the positive real numbers.

===Square===
Let <math>Q = \R_{> 0} \times \R_{> 0},</math> the first quadrant of the Cartesian plane. The quadrant itself is divided into four parts by the line <math>L = \{(x,y): x = y \}</math> and the standard hyperbola <math>H = \{(x,y): xy = 1 \}.</math>

The <math>L \cup H</math> forms a trident while <math>L \cap H = (1, 1)</math> is the central point. It is the identity element of two [[one-parameter group]]s that intersect there:
<math display="block">\{\left\{\left(e^a, \ e^a\right): a \in R \right\}, \times \} \text{ on } L \quad \text{ and } \quad \{\left\{\left(e^a, \ e^{-a}\right): a \in R\right\},\times \} \text{ on } H.</math>

Since <math>\R_{> 0}</math> is a [[Group (mathematics)|group]], <math>Q</math> is a [[direct product of groups]]. The one-parameter subgroups ''L'' and ''H'' in ''Q'' profile the activity in the product, and <math>L \times H</math> is a resolution of the types of group action.

The realms of business and science abound in ratios, and any change in ratios draws attention. The study refers to [[hyperbolic coordinates]] in ''Q''. Motion against the ''L'' axis indicates a change in the [[geometric mean]] <math>\sqrt{xy},</math> while a change along ''H'' indicates a new [[hyperbolic angle]].
